proof.text: Identify the quotient of ULift A by the lifted generator ideal power with ULift of A/I^(n+1), using Ideal.quotientEquiv and ha. Compare its constant ring sheaf with the finite-functions ring sheaf using finiteRingComparison and the proved constantComparison_isIso helper from completed constant sheaf reduction. Naturality on constant sections identifies all transition maps, giving quotientSystemIso. The argument also applies to zero rings and to the zero or unit ideal.

The forgetful functor from commutative ring sheaves to ring sheaves preserves the inverse limit. Transport quotientSystemIso through the preserved-limit comparison and lift along the fully faithful forgetful functor to obtain completionRingIso. Projection identities and equality on locally constant sections identify the actual completed scalar map with the constant-completion coefficient map.

Construct the normalized scalar-extension morphism from the constant quotient module to its restricted regular ring sheaf. Define the map from the constant module by the constant ring unit, then apply constant-module sheafification and the scalar-tensor adjunction. It sends s tensor the constant class x to p(s) times the constant class x. Apply completed_constant_algebra_flat_quotients over ULift A to show it is invertible. Transport through quotientRingIso to the actual finite module. The normalized regular-unit isomorphism and tensor naturality show that its composite with the quotient map is reconstructionQuotientUnit.

Both extended single complexes are concentrated in degree zero. Assemble the degree-zero quotient-module isomorphism and the unique isomorphisms between zero objects in other degrees into a complex isomorphism. Choose c using the degree-zero unit-complex isomorphism followed by the normalized regular-unit isomorphism. Compute the degree-zero component, cancel the extension and single-complex isomorphisms, and use right-unitor naturality and the defining ordinary-unit projection formula to obtain the required normalized equality.
